info.bio:
Ian Dury, formado en el pub rock londinense del barrio de Kilburn y aquejado de poliomelitis.
Se curte zurrando la badana en los pubs de la zona y mamando rock, funk , blues y Jazz.
Su primera banda es Kilburn & the High roads y posteriormente forma ya con su nombre de cabecero.
 Ian Dury & the Blockheads y mas tarde Ian Dury & the music Students.
Sus discos estrella son "New boots & panties" con temazos del calibre "Wake up & make love with me" o la emblematica "sex & drugs & Rock & roll" .

podcast.title: Childhood Polio and Paralysis
podcast.body: Ian Dury contracted polio at the age of seven in 1949, likely from a public swimming pool, and subsequently spent a year and a half in the hospital. The disease resulted in paralysis on his left side, causing his shoulder, arm, and leg to wither, yet this severe disability did not deter him from pursuing a musical career during the punk era. "He contracted polio at the age of seven in 1949, probably from a public swimming pool."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Colorectal Cancer and Death
podcast.body: Ian Dury's health problems continued throughout his life, culminating in a diagnosis of colorectal cancer in 1996. The cancer eventually metastasized, leading to his death on March 27, 2000, at the age of 57. "He was diagnosed with colorectal cancer in 1996."

xref.title: First Canadian Band to Sign to Stiff Records – Power Pop Side of Vancouver Punk
xref.body: The Pointed Sticks formed in Vancouver in 1978, five former members overlapping with D.O.A. and the Subhumans. Their sound was more melodic and power pop-leaning than their contemporaries — five members singing harmonies was unusual in punk. Their name came from a Monty Python sketch about self-defense against pointed sticks. They became the first Canadian band to sign to Stiff Records in the UK, home to the Damned, Nick Lowe, Elvis Costello, and Ian Dury. Several strong singles and one album followed. Their relative accessibility broadened the audience for Vancouver punk. "Stiff Records, one of the groundbreaking indie labels in the UK."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Ian Dury's Polio and Cancer
xref.body: Ian Dury contracted polio at about seven years old and lived with its effects for the rest of his life. He was later diagnosed with colorectal cancer, which spread to his liver, and he died on March 27th, 2000.
